chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about water in which beasts urinate, dogs lap, and the person in janabah bathes. He said: If it is the measure of a kurr, nothing makes it najis.

key_terms.الدَّوَابُّ: beasts or riding animals that may urinate in the water
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah
key_terms.الْكِلَابُ: dogs that lap from the water
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the subject of the purity ruling
key_terms.كُرٍّ: the prescribed large measure of water in fiqh
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: renders it najis or ritually impure

ai.seo_question: Does water become najis if dogs lap from it or animals urinate in it when it is a kurr amount?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water and ritual purity. It states that when water reaches the measure of a kurr, it is not rendered najis by such contact as animals urinating in it, dogs lapping from it, or a junub bathing in it.
